html:
SMTO-LLM-0097 — The model didn't start answering in time

GUID: 25ec49b4-d159-4ede-b9bf-794eafb47cb3
Slug: model-generation-startup-timeout
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • SMTO waited for the model to start its answer, but nothing arrived before the time limit, only signals that the connection was still open. No action ran, and earlier finished work is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running your model service is on, not busy with other work, and has finished loading the model. A busy or still-loading service can stay silent past SMTO's waiting limit.
  2. Open the stopped task and select Resume. Earlier finished work is kept, and the waiting step starts again from scratch.
  3. If your model is often slow to start, open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card and Limits and recovery, raise Request timeout, select Save Main, and start a new task. New tasks use the longer wait; a resumed task keeps the time limits it started with.

What success looks like

  • Activity appears in the task soon after it starts, and the task moves on.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs your model service. Don't raise Recovery timeout, Recovery deadline or budgets for this; Request timeout is the setting that controls this wait.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • No observable generation (reasoning, answer text, tool arguments or an increasing progress counter) arrived within the request timeout; heartbeats do not extend this startup wait, and this is not evidence of repetitive reasoning.

What this means

  • The absolute startup wait elapsed before the first meaningful reasoning, answer, tool arguments or increasing generation counter. Heartbeats cannot extend startup. This is not evidence of repeated reasoning; provider queueing or a stalled service may require investigation.

Why this can happen

  • No observable generation began before the configured model timeout; the underlying service cause is not established.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the reported reason and effective settings.

How to fix it

  • Check provider health and queueing (busy server, cold model load or a stalled worker) at that time. The startup wait equals the request timeout (capped by Capability selection timeout during capability selection). If startup legitimately takes longer, increase Request timeout under Limits and recovery for the role in Settings › Setup › Model routing for new tasks; Resume starts a fresh attempt and preserves earlier completed work.
  • Check provider health and the model request timeout. If a cold or queued provider legitimately needs longer startup, increase that timeout for a new task. Resume preserves earlier completed work.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open model settings: model-configuration / llm_timeout_seconds. Applies to: new task.
  • Start a new task after changing this setting. Active and resumed tasks retain their captured values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Explicit Resume starts a fresh episode and retains completed tool receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The provider begins observable generation before its startup allowance expires.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • The current decision is rejected before tool authorization when enforcement applies; earlier results are not replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
